finding: cuOpt arm64/CUDA-13 is NOW available and runs on the GB10. API changed since Phase 0 (set_task_locations → set_order_locations). Crossover at ~100 locations: cuOpt GPU wins at scale, OR-Tools CPU wins below 100 locations.
benchmark_type: VRP (vehicle routing problem, 1 vehicle, symmetric distance matrix)
solver_settings: cuOpt: 0.1s time limit. OR-Tools: PATH_CHEAPEST_ARC default.
key_observations: cuOpt has ~100-120ms fixed GPU overhead (kernel launch + data transfer)
OR-Tools scales super-linearly (~O(n²)); cuOpt scales sublinearly after fixed cost
Crossover at ~100 locations — below that, OR-Tools CPU is faster
At 500 locations, cuOpt is 27.8x faster than OR-Tools
Default cuOpt time_limit is effectively infinite (3.4e38) — must set explicitly

prototype_impact.main_optimizer: Uses OR-Tools GLOP for transportation LP (select_ortools_lanes in common.py). cuOpt is a VRP solver, NOT an LP solver — it does not replace this. OR-Tools LP stays.
prototype_impact.smoke_endpoint: cuopt_smoke.py now works with updated API (set_order_locations). cuOpt detected and usable at /cuopt/solve when installed.
prototype_impact.lane_count: Prototype max is ~152 lanes (from scale study). This is below the crossover — OR-Tools CPU is the right choice.
prototype_impact.recommendation: Keep OR-Tools as the lane-routing engine. cuOpt is available for future VRP use cases (fleet routing with 100+ stops) if needed.

dependency_notes.numpy_downgrade: cuopt-cu13 requires numpy 2.4.x (container had 2.5.1). Torch 2.13.0+cu130 works with 2.4.6.
dependency_notes.not_in_requirements: cuopt-cu13 is NOT added to requirements-api.txt — it's optional and adds ~28 packages. The smoke endpoint falls back to OR-Tools gracefully.
